sentences.en: Come cheer up my lads, tis to glory we steer, to add something more to this wonderful year.
sentences.zh: 来吧，小伙子们，振作起来，我们正驶向荣耀，为这美妙的一年增添光彩。

sentences.en: To honour, we call you, as free men, not slaves.
sentences.zh: 我们呼唤你们去争取荣誉，作为自由人，而非奴隶。

sentences.en: For who are so free as the sons of the waves?
sentences.zh: 因为谁能比海之子更自由呢？

sentences.en: Heart of ochre are our ships, jolly tars are our men.
sentences.zh: 我们的船身坚如磐石，我们的水手英勇无畏。

sentences.en: We always are ready.
sentences.zh: 我们时刻准备着。

sentences.en: Steady, boys, steady.
sentences.zh: 稳住，小伙子们，稳住。

sentences.en: We'll fight and we'll conquer again and again.
sentences.zh: 我们将一次又一次地战斗，一次又一次地征服。

sentences.en: We ne'er see our foes, but we wish them to stay.
sentences.zh: 我们从未见过敌人，但我们希望他们留下来。

sentences.en: They never see us, but they wish us a way.
sentences.zh: 他们从未见过我们，但他们希望我们离去。

sentences.en: If they run, why, we follow and run them ashore.
sentences.zh: 如果他们逃跑，好吧，我们就追赶他们，把他们赶上岸。

sentences.en: For if they won't fight us, what can we do more?
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们不愿与我们交战，我们还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: So, Tom Holland, that's Heart of Oak, written in 1759 after the Battle of Quiberon Bay and sung a few hours aboard the victory before the
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆·霍兰，这就是《橡木之心》，写于 1759 年基伯龙湾海战之后，并在几小时后于“胜利号”上演唱，就在

sentences.en: Great Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.
sentences.zh: 1805 年特拉法尔加海战之前。

sentences.en: So, one of the great anthems of the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 这是皇家海军最伟大的赞歌之一。

sentences.en: And you have wanted to do a podcast about Trafalgar since we started The Rest Is History, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 自从我们开始做《历史的余味》以来，你就一直想做一期关于特拉法尔加的播客，对吧？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is the perfect week to be doing it because Friday, the 21st of October, is Trafalgar Day, the day on which the battle was actually fought.
sentences.zh: 这一周做这期节目再合适不过了，因为 10 月 21 日星期五是特拉法尔加日，也就是那场战役实际发生的日期。

sentences.en: So, we were originally going to do one episode, weren't we?
sentences.zh: 我们原本打算只做一期，对吧？

sentences.en: We were.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: On Trafalgar.
sentences.zh: 关于特拉法尔加的。

sentences.en: And I went away on holiday and I started reading about it and I read about it and I read about it and I read about it.
sentences.zh: 后来我去度假了，开始阅读相关资料，读啊读，读啊读，读啊读。

sentences.en: And I sent you a text saying, I think we should do two episodes.
sentences.zh: 然后我给你发了条短信，说我觉得我们应该做两期。

sentences.en: Well, we're now going to be doing three episodes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在我们要录三期了。

sentences.en: So, we're going to talk about today, a world at war, the background to this great battle.
sentences.zh: 所以，今天我们要谈谈那个战火纷飞的世界，这场伟大战役的背景。

sentences.en: Napoleon against Nelson, France against
sentences.zh: 拿破仑对阵纳尔逊，法国对阵

sentences.en: Britain, the elephant against the whale, this great clash.
sentences.zh: 英国，大象对阵鲸鱼，这场伟大的碰撞。

sentences.en: Next time, we will look at the build up to the battle.
sentences.zh: 下一次，我们将探讨战役的准备阶段。

sentences.en: And then on Friday, the 21st of October, Trafalgar Day, we will look at the actual battle itself.
sentences.zh: 然后在 10 月 21 日星期五，即特拉法尔加日，我们将审视这场战役本身。

sentences.en: And Dominic, I have gone on record, haven't I, as saying that I'm not particularly interested in rope or ships or mizzenmasts or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我曾公开表示过，我不怎么对绳索、船只、后桅帆或其他类似的东西感兴趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because this is in the context of the novels of Patrick O'Brien that you refused to read.
sentences.zh: 因为这是在你拒绝阅读帕特里克·奥布莱恩小说的情况下说的。

sentences.en: I now want to recant.
sentences.zh: 我现在想收回前言。

sentences.en: I want to recant.
sentences.zh: 我想收回前言。

sentences.en: Oh, what a moment.
sentences.zh: 哦，真是个历史性的时刻。

sentences.en: I think this is an absolutely thrilling story.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个绝对扣人心弦的故事。

sentences.en: I think it's the great epic of British history, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这是英国历史上最伟大的史诗。

sentences.en: And when I say epic, I mean in the sense that, the Homeric sense.
sentences.zh: 当我提到史诗时，我是指荷马史诗那种意义上的。

sentences.en: Nelson is a kind of a disinfigure, endlessly sweeping the seas.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊就像是一个不朽的化身，无休止地横扫海洋。

sentences.en: He's on the sea at two years at a time.
sentences.zh: 他曾连续两年在海上漂泊。

sentences.en: And then at Trafalgar, Byron called him Britannia's god of war.
sentences.zh: 而在特拉法尔加，拜伦称他为“不列颠的战神”。

sentences.en: He is a kind of great agent of annihilation, a kind of terrifying figure, really, who dies at the moment of his triumph, becomes the great martyr of the navy.
sentences.zh: 他确实是一位伟大的毁灭代理人，一个真正令人恐惧的人物，他在胜利的瞬间死去，成为了海军最伟大的殉道者。

sentences.en: Well, that obviously, we'll come to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然，我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But that martyrdom is absolutely central to the story.
sentences.zh: 但那种殉道精神对于这个故事来说是绝对核心的。

sentences.en: It's an astonishing story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人惊叹的故事。

sentences.en: And it's a story in which the stakes could not be higher.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个故事中，赌注高得不能再高了。

sentences.en: For Britain, it's about national survival.
sentences.zh: 对于英国来说，这关乎国家存亡。

sentences.en: And for France, it's about the opportunity to knock
sentences.zh: 而对于法国来说，这是一个彻底击垮

sentences.en: Britain out permanently, and thereby secure a permanent French supremacy over Europe.
sentences.zh: 英国的机会，从而确保法国在欧洲的永久霸权。

sentences.en: So huge, huge stakes.
sentences.zh: 所以，赌注非常、非常巨大。

sentences.en: But there is a debate about Trafalgar, and how decisive it actually is.
sentences.zh: 但关于特拉法尔加及其决定性意义，一直存在争议。

sentences.en: So there are historians who say it didn't really change anything particularly.
sentences.zh: 有些历史学家认为它并没有真正改变什么特别的东西。

sentences.en: What's your view on that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Because I actually think that it's probably the most decisive battle of the 19th century, for reasons that we'll come to in due course.
sentences.zh: 因为我实际上认为它可能是 19 世纪最具决定性的战役，原因我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: Yeah, I probably agree with you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是的，汤姆，我可能同意你的看法。

sentences.en: I think there are some battles that do feel like decisive showdowns or turning points.
sentences.zh: 我认为有些战役确实感觉像是决定性的对决或转折点。

sentences.en: So, I mean, naval battles, you know, the Battle of Actium, maybe, or the Battle of Midway or something.
sentences.zh: 我是说，海战，比如亚克兴海战，或者中途岛海战之类的。

sentences.en: And I think Trafalgar is obviously in the very top rank of those.
sentences.zh: 我认为特拉法尔加显然位列其中最高级别。

sentences.en: Because I think what it does, I mean, we'll come on to talk about the geopolitical ramifications later.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为它的作用——我们稍后会谈到地缘政治的影响——

sentences.en: But I think what Trafalgar does is it ultimately, you could argue, it makes it impossible for the French to win, to knock Britain out of the Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 但我认为特拉法尔加最终使得法国人不可能赢得战争，不可能将英国踢出拿破仑战争。

sentences.en: Had Trafalgar gone otherwise, had the French landed in Britain, and maybe not invaded,
sentences.zh: 如果特拉法尔加的结果不同，如果法国人登陆了英国，也许没有占领，

sentences.en: but maybe smashed up Britain's dockyards, smashed up London, and so on, made it impossible for
sentences.zh: 但也许摧毁了英国的造船厂，摧毁了伦敦等等，使得

sentences.en: Britain to continue to fight at sea.
sentences.zh: 英国无法继续在海上作战。

sentences.en: That would have had enormous ramifications for the war in
sentences.zh: 那将对欧洲的战争产生巨大的影响，

sentences.en: Europe, but also in the long term, over the course of the 19th century, for the imperial balance of power.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，在 19 世纪的进程中，也会对帝国权力平衡产生巨大影响。

sentences.en: And I would say Trafalgar ensures that Britain will be the world's largest commercial and imperial power for the next 100 years or so.
sentences.zh: 我会说特拉法尔加确保了英国在未来 100 年左右的时间里成为世界上最强大的商业和帝国强权。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对正确。

sentences.en: And I think so there's a paradox there, which is that perhaps it's less decisive as a
sentences.zh: 我认为这里存在一个悖论，即它作为拿破仑战争中的一场战役，

sentences.en: battle in the Napoleonic Wars than it is as a battle in the broader context of the 19th century,
sentences.zh: 可能不如它在 19 世纪更广阔的背景下作为一场战役那样具有决定性，

sentences.en: which is kind of a seeming paradox that perhaps we can look at when we actually come to the battle itself.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个悖论，也许当我们真正谈到战役本身时可以探讨一下。

sentences.en: But just to jump in, though, Tom, I agree with you about the Homeric epic.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，我想插一句，我同意你关于荷马史诗的看法。

sentences.en: And I think the fact that the figure at the centre of the struggle, I mean, it's that strange thing, isn't it, where there are two figures who everybody knows, Nelson and Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 我认为处于斗争中心的人物这一事实——这很奇怪，不是吗？有两个大家都知道的人物，纳尔逊和拿破仑。

sentences.en: Napoleon is never there, but his shadow hangs over the whole story.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑从未亲临现场，但他的阴影笼罩着整个故事。

sentences.en: But Nelson is there in a very intimate kind of way on the deck of the victory, risking his life.
sentences.zh: 而纳尔逊却以一种非常亲密的方式出现在“胜利号”的甲板上，冒着生命危险。

sentences.en: And of course, it's the fact that he dies in the moment of apotheosis that turns this into more than just an ordinary battle.
sentences.zh: 当然，正是他在神化时刻死去的事实，使这不仅仅是一场普通的战役。

sentences.en: It turns it into an absolute, I hate to use the word because it's such a terrible cliche, but it turns it into, dare I say, an iconic moment in British national history.
sentences.zh: 它使它变成了一个——我讨厌用这个词，因为它太陈词滥调了——但它变成了一个，我敢说，英国国家历史上的标志性时刻。

sentences.en: But there's one other thing that I think makes Trafalgar so interesting.
sentences.zh: 但还有一件事我认为让特拉法尔加如此有趣。

sentences.en: And I know at this point, you'll roll your eyes because you're terrified that I'm going to start talking about
sentences.zh: 我知道此时你会翻白眼，因为你担心我会开始谈论

sentences.en: 17th century finance.
sentences.zh: 17 世纪的金融。

sentences.en: But I think Trafalgar is the culmination of all kinds of political, financial, economic, cultural processes that have been working themselves out for more than 100 years.
sentences.zh: 但我认为特拉法尔加是各种政治、金融、经济、文化进程的结晶，这些进程已经运作了 100 多年。

sentences.en: And it's a brilliant window, actually, into talking about Britain as a state since its creation.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它是一个绝佳的窗口，可以用来谈论英国自建国以来的国家状态。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Well, so Andrew Lambert, great naval historian, biographer of Nelson, describes the
sentences.zh: 嗯，伟大的海军历史学家、纳尔逊的传记作者安德鲁·兰伯特将

sentences.en: Royal Navy as the most successful fighting service the world had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 皇家海军描述为世界上有史以来最成功的战斗部队。

sentences.en: Adam Nicholson, who wrote a brilliant book, Men of Honor, about Trafalgar, calls it the most effective maritime killing machine in the world.
sentences.zh: 写过关于特拉法尔加的杰作《荣誉之士》的亚当·尼科尔森称其为世界上最有效的海上杀戮机器。

sentences.en: And I think that the Royal Navy obviously lies at the heart of the story.
sentences.zh: 我认为皇家海军显然是这个故事的核心。

sentences.en: And as you say, I think we're so familiar with the idea of Britannia ruling the waves, the idea that Britain was a naval power, that it's good to look at how that came about,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我认为我们对“不列颠统治海洋”的观念，即英国是一个海军强国的观念太熟悉了，所以看看它是如何形成的很有意义，

sentences.en: because actually there was nothing inevitable about it for centuries and centuries.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上几个世纪以来，这并非必然。

sentences.en: Britain did not rule the waves.
sentences.zh: 英国并没有统治海洋。

sentences.en: I mean, it was hopeless when it came to kind of controlling its own waters, let alone the waters of Europe and the world beyond.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在控制自己的水域方面，它简直无可救药，更不用说欧洲和世界其他地方的水域了。

sentences.en: And the story of how that happens is obviously an absolutely fundamental part of Trafalgar and indeed the entire Napoleonic conflict.
sentences.zh: 关于它是如何发生的，显然是特拉法尔加乃至整个拿破仑冲突的一个绝对基本的部分。

sentences.en: But I think before we get to the Royal Navy and indeed the French and Spanish fleets that fight on the other side of
sentences.zh: 但在我们谈到皇家海军，以及在特拉法尔加另一方作战的法国和西班牙舰队之前，

sentences.en: Trafalgar, we should just set the scene in the geopolitics of what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我们应该先设定一下当时地缘政治的背景。

sentences.en: So 1805 is the year, I suppose it ranks like 1588, the year of the Spanish Armada, 1940, the year of the Battle of
sentences.zh: 所以 1805 年，我想它和 1588 年（西班牙无敌舰队之年）、1940 年（不列颠战役之年）一样，

sentences.en: Britain, as a year when Britain faces invasion by a foreign force.
sentences.zh: 是英国面临外国势力入侵威胁的一年。

sentences.en: The question of how credible a threat that actually was is something that we'll come to in due course.
sentences.zh: 这种威胁到底有多可信，是我们稍后会讨论的问题。

sentences.en: But that is part of the mythology, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这确实是神话的一部分，不是吗？

sentences.en: That 1805, Napoleon could have invaded Britain.
sentences.zh: 即 1805 年，拿破仑本可以入侵英国。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So to give people a sense of the sort of the lie of the land, Britain and France have fought something like seven major wars, I think, since the 1690s or so.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家了解当时的情况，自 1690 年代左右以来，英国和法国已经打了大约七场主要战争。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in France, they call it the second hundred years war.
sentences.zh: 所以在法国，他们称之为“第二次百年战争”。

sentences.en: So the first hundred years war in the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 第一次百年战争是在中世纪。

sentences.en: But this is a kind of ongoing process of conflicts that just run and run and run.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种持续不断的冲突过程，没完没了。

sentences.en: And they are increasingly, aren't they, world wars.
sentences.zh: 而且它们越来越像是世界大战，不是吗？

sentences.en: So they're wars that take place in multiple theatres, you know, thousands of miles apart, and very often very largely kind of, I mean,
sentences.zh: 它们是在多个战区进行的战争，你知道，相隔数千英里，而且通常很大程度上，我的意思是，

sentences.en: there's there are elements on land, but the Navy is always hugely important.
sentences.zh: 虽然有陆地上的因素，但海军总是极其重要。

sentences.en: And this is the latest one.
sentences.zh: 这就是最近的一场。

sentences.en: And it's been raging since the early 1790s.
sentences.zh: 而且它从 1790 年代初就开始肆虐了。

sentences.en: It's sort of off and on, there are sort of stop start.
sentences.zh: 断断续续的，有点走走停停。

sentences.en: But I think you can see it all as one kind of continuous campaign, ultimately, can't you?
sentences.zh: 但我认为你可以把它看作是一场持续的战役，最终是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: And Britain is constantly trying to enlist to do what it's always done, trying to enlist
sentences.zh: 英国一直在努力做它一直做的事情，试图招募

sentences.en: continental coalitions against Napoleon, because one of the strange things about Britain is Britain
sentences.zh: 欧洲大陆的联盟来对抗拿破仑，因为英国奇怪的一点是，英国

sentences.en: is a world power, but militarily and on land, it is not really much of a yeah, it is a pygmy,
sentences.zh: 是一个世界强国，但在军事和陆地上，它真的不是什么——是的，它是一个侏儒，

sentences.en: because for reasons we'll go on to discuss, Britain has always invested in its navy rather than its army.
sentences.zh: 因为出于我们稍后会讨论的原因，英国一直投资于海军而不是陆军。

sentences.en: So that means Britain needs allies, but it also needs to uphold its side of the bargain, which is to kind of, you know, maintain its naval supremacy.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着英国需要盟友，但也需要履行其职责，即维持其海军霸权。

sentences.en: Napoleon, so he faces the same strategic dilemma that the successive French administrations have faced.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑面临着历届法国政府所面临的同样的战略困境。

sentences.en: They've always struggled to raise enough money to fight on land and at sea.
sentences.zh: 他们一直难以筹集足够的资金在陆地和海上作战。

sentences.en: So France is always ending these wars, whatever the result of the war, France is always ending these wars bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 所以法国总是以破产告终，无论战争结果如何。

sentences.en: But Napoleon, because he's, I mean, he's he's ruthless, he's literally, I mean, he's rapacious, he plunders countries he occupies.
sentences.zh: 但拿破仑，因为他——我的意思是，他冷酷无情，他简直是贪婪，他掠夺他占领的国家。

sentences.en: He poses a kind of threat to Britain, I would say, Tom, that no previous French administration has ever posed.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为他给英国带来的威胁是之前任何法国政府都未曾带来的。

sentences.en: Don't you?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Wouldn't you agree?
sentences.zh: 你不同意吗？

sentences.en: This is a, this is a kind of an existential challenge on a scale that goes beyond the challenges of, I don't know, the, well, certainly the nine years
sentences.zh: 这是一种存在主义的挑战，其规模超出了，我不知道，嗯，当然超出了九年战争、

sentences.en: war, the war of the Spanish succession, or some of these previous conflicts.
sentences.zh: 西班牙王位继承战争或之前的一些冲突。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Because what, and it's not just Napoleon, it's the revolutionary wars as well.

sentences.en: But in the long run, it kind of wins the competition.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，它在某种程度上赢得了这场竞争。

sentences.en: Because all the time it is losing, the Royal Navy is improving, is modernizing, is learning from its opponents.
sentences.zh: 因为在不断失败的同时，皇家海军也在进步、现代化，并从对手身上学习。

sentences.en: So, by the 1660, when you have the restoration, it is already much larger.
sentences.zh: 所以到了1660年，也就是复辟时期，它的规模已经大得多了。

sentences.en: It has two admirals in particular, so Blake and Monk, who are very much into kind of, we need to be more disciplined.
sentences.zh: 当时有两位特别的将军，布莱克和蒙克，他们非常强调“我们需要更强的纪律性”。

sentences.en: It can't be the sort of shambles that it has been for most of our history.
sentences.zh: 不能再像我们历史上大部分时间那样一团糟了。

sentences.en: And the government is prepared to finance that.
sentences.zh: 政府也准备为此提供资金。

sentences.en: And that continues.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续下去。

sentences.en: So, it's a great example, actually, the continuity between the Cromwellian period and the restoration, because that continues under Charles II.
sentences.zh: 所以，这实际上是克伦威尔时期与复辟时期之间连续性的一个绝佳例子，因为这种情况在查理二世统治下得以延续。

sentences.en: And James II was Lord High Admiral during the restoration period.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯二世在复辟时期担任海军大臣。

sentences.en: He's very much all about the Navy.
sentences.zh: 他非常重视海军。

sentences.zh: 所以，他们在复辟时期特别做了两件事。

sentences.en: So, one is you have peeps and administration, so the creation of a kind of bureaucracy.
sentences.zh: 一是皮普斯和行政管理，即建立了一种官僚体系。

sentences.en: And the other is professionalization.
sentences.zh: 另一是专业化。

sentences.zh: 实际上是在查理二世统治下，海军中尉必须通过考试。

sentences.en: And if you think about the British Army, so right into the 19th century, it's still a very amateur way of life where you buy your way in.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看英国陆军，一直到19世纪，它仍然是一种非常业余的生活方式，你可以花钱买官。

sentences.en: So, in the Navy, Charles II describes the Navy as a trade, a very telling word.
sentences.zh: 而在海军中，查理二世将海军描述为一种“行业”（trade），这是一个非常说明问题的词。

sentences.en: In other words, it's not, you know, it's something, you learn a trade, and you have to pass an exam to do it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你得学习一门手艺，而且必须通过考试才能胜任。

sentences.en: So, it's a professional enterprise.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个专业的企业。

sentences.en: And then when you get to the end of the 17th century,
sentences.zh: 然后当你进入17世纪末，

sentences.en: William of Orange and Mary and Anne, obviously now you're in competition with the French.
sentences.zh: 威廉三世、玛丽和安妮女王时期，显然你现在是在与法国人竞争。

sentences.en: So, rather than the Dutch, you're now facing the French who are a real, you know, they are the superpower.
sentences.zh: 所以，不再是荷兰人，你现在面对的是法国人，他们是真正的超级大国。

sentences.en: And the only way England and Scotland and then Britain can compete is through finance.
sentences.zh: 英格兰、苏格兰乃至后来的英国，唯一能与之竞争的方法就是通过金融。

sentences.en: So, William brings over, you know, these sort of Dutch financial techniques.
sentences.zh: 所以，威廉带来了这些荷兰式的金融技术。

sentences.en: And now they're being applied on a much grander scale.
sentences.zh: 现在它们正以更大的规模被应用。

sentences.en: So, the classic one is the Bank of England.

sentences.en: England is locked in this sort of long struggle against Louis XIV's France.

sentences.en: Right away, the Bank of England raises more than a million pounds and an absolutely astronomical sum of money by the standards of the day.
sentences.zh: 英格兰银行立即筹集了超过一百万英镑，这在当时的标准下是一笔天文数字。

sentences.en: And more than half of that, Tom, was spent on the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 而且其中超过一半，汤姆，都花在了皇家海军身上。

sentences.zh: 所以，金融和海军力量是绝对交织在一起的。

sentences.en: And in fact, even the public are financing the Navy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，连公众都在为海军融资。

sentences.en: will give you a return of 6% a year.
sentences.zh: 每年给你6%的回报。

sentences.en: And that presumably is seen as being patriotic, the patriotic option.

sentences.en: Absolutely.

sentences.en: Absolutely.
